title: SLTMobitel company history (Wikipedia)
text: SLTMobitel (Sri Lanka Telecom and its mobile subsidiary Mobitel) is headquartered in Colombo, Sri Lanka. Its history goes back to 1858, when the first telegraphic circuit between Galle and Colombo was established. Sri Lanka Telecom was corporatised in 1991 and privatised in 2000 in collaboration with Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation (NTT). In 2008 NTT sold its stake in SLT to Global Telecommunications Holdings N.V. of the Netherlands. According to the article, the Government of Sri Lanka holds 49.50 percent of the shares and Global Telecommunications Holdings N.V. holds 44.98 percent, with the rest held by the public. The company is listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange under the symbol SLTL.N0000. Mobitel was incorporated in 1993 as the third mobile telephone provider in Sri Lanka, originally as a collaboration between Sri Lanka Telecom and Telstra, and has been wholly owned by SLT since November 2002. As of 2024, SLTMobitel was Sri Lanka's second largest mobile network operator with 7.1 million subscribers. Notable subsidiaries include Mobitel (Pvt) Ltd and eChannelling PLC.

title: SLTMobitel services and network milestones (Wikipedia)
text: SLTMobitel offers fixed and wireless telephony, ADSL2+ and VDSL2 broadband, fibre broadband (the article mentions 300 Mbps and 1 Gbps), 4G LTE, Wi-Fi, and prepaid and postpaid mobile services. Mobitel launched a 2.5G GSM/EDGE network in 2004 and, in December 2007, the first Super 3.5G HSPA network in South Asia. In January 2014 it demonstrated a 4G LTE fixed wireless service. Mobitel launched its mobile money service, called mCash, in November 2013.

title: Sri Lanka Telecom and Mobitel join forces under one brand (official press release)
text: Sri Lanka Telecom (SLT) and Mobitel unveiled a unified brand identity, SLT-MOBITEL, on 1 January 2021, bringing SLT's and Mobitel's products and services (fixed line, mobile, broadband, internet TV and other services) under a single brand. The stated aim was to strengthen the brand equity of SLT-MOBITEL by combining the goodwill of both into one strong brand with digitalization at its core, and to position the group as the nation's leading ICT solutions provider supporting the country's digitalization. The release describes SLT as operating for over 163 years, and Mobitel as the first operator in South Asia to trial 5G on a commercial mobile network.

title: SLT and Mobitel launch unified brand identity (Daily Mirror, January 2021)
text: Daily Mirror reported on 4 January 2021 that Sri Lanka Telecom and its subsidiary Mobitel brought all their products and services under one brand identity, SLT-MOBITEL. The unification was expected to save about Rs. 100 million a year in advertising and corporate communication expenses and about Rs. 1 billion a year in sales expenses. Planned outcomes included a unified contact centre, new packages under the unified brand such as combined fibre and broadband offers, and sharing some back end operations such as the customer relationship management database, while the two companies kept separate managements within the group. The article repeats that Mobitel launched the first commercial 4.5G/4G+ mobile network in South Asia in 2018 and was the first network in South Asia to showcase 5G over a mobile network.

title: SLT-MOBITEL trials 5G-Advanced (official news)
text: SLT-MOBITEL conducted Sri Lanka's first 5G-Advanced (5G-A) trial on 12 January 2025, reaching speeds of over 5 Gbps. SLT-MOBITEL had also deployed a 5G pre-commercial trial network in five cities: Colombo, Kandy, Anuradhapura, Galle and Jaffna. Customers need a 5G-ready device that is compatible with the network to use it.

title: SLT-Mobitel launches commercial 5G (December 2025)
text: In December 2025 Dialog Axiata and SLT-Mobitel launched commercial 5G services in Sri Lanka, after the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (TRCSL) completed its 5G spectrum auction. SLT-Mobitel secured spectrum blocks in the 3500 MHz band. Earlier in 2025 Mobitel had been trialling 5G-Advanced technology. CGTN reported that SLT-Mobitel held its launch at One Galle Face Mall in Colombo, demonstrating high speed internet, low latency connectivity, real time gaming and augmented and virtual reality uses.

title: How to make a complaint about a telecom service (TRCSL)
text: The Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka (TRCSL) says consumers must first take a complaint to their own service provider, keep a record of the complaint and any correspondence, allow the provider reasonable time to act, and follow up by phone if needed. If the provider does not address the problem adequately within a reasonable time, the consumer may submit a written complaint to the Commission. TRCSL lists the customer care contacts of operators: Mobitel (Pvt) Ltd on 1717 or 2330550, email info@mobitel.lk, and SLT PLC on 1212. TRCSL itself is at No. 276, Elvitigala Mawatha, Colombo 08, telephone +94 11 2689345 or +94 11 2689341, email cc@trc.gov.lk.
